ucose-lowering medications target different aspects of the 
pathogenesis of T2DM—insulin resistance at the cellular level, 
incretin system defects, endogenous insulin deficiency, elevated 
levels of glucagon, and excessive hepatic glucose release. Be-
cause the mechanisms of action differ, the medications can be 
used alone or in combination. Table 30-5 lists the generic and 
brand names of glucose-lowering medications and their princi-
pal sites of action for persons with T2DM.
Biguanides.  Metformin is the most widely used first-line 
type 2 medication. It suppresses hepatic glucose production, is 
not associated with hypoglycemia, may cause small weight 
losses when therapy begins, and is relatively inexpensive. The
